recipes.name: K-Dub's Alfredo Ravioli Bake
ingredients_raw: 3 skinless, boneless chicken breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat an oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a rolling boil; boil the ravioli until it floats and the filling is hot, 6 to 8 minutes; drain.

Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat. Add the chicken to the skillet, season with the Italian seasoning, and cook and stir until the chicken is no longer pink in the middle, about 15 minutes.

Spread about 1/2 cup Alfredo sauce into the bottom of the prepared baking dish. Arrange enough ravioli over the sauce to cover the bottom of the dish completely. Top the ravioli with about 1/2 of the cooked chicken. Sprinkle 1 cup mozzarella cheese over the chicken; season with salt and pepper. Repeat the layers until all ingredients are used.

Bake in the preheated oven until heated through completely and the mozzarella cheese is melted, about 25 minutes. Sprinkle the Parmesan evenly over the top of the dish; return to the oven for 5 more minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: K-Dub's Alfredo Ravioli Bake
raw_recipe.description: This baked pasta dish features prepared ravioli and Alfredo sauce combined with chicken and mozzarella cheese for an easy and delicious weeknight meal.

review.reviewBody: DELICIOUS! I did omit the chicken, but added some sauteed mushrooms, onion and garlic in with the alfredo sauce that I made homemade. Also added a layer of homemade pesto in the middle, and that was an awesome addition. I loved the flavors/richness of this dish and the fact that you can add whatever you like and come out with a simple, yet tasty meal. Made this a bit ahead of time and just baked it when I was ready, and that worked out well. I servd this w/ a salad and garlic bread. A definite keeper! Thanks for sharing. :)

Loved your casserole and have wonderful leftovers to enjoy. I used 4 small chx breasts, totalling 1 lb. After sauteeing, I used the same pan to sautee 4 minced garlic cloves, 1/4 chopped onion and a 6 oz bag of baby spinach. Mixed all with the cooked cubed chx and proceeded to build the casserole. I opted to use tortallini as we had recently had ravioli for dinner. I used Classico Lite Asiago Romano Alfredo Sauce - very yummy. Topped with pecorino romano. Definitely will be making this dish again! Thanks K-Dub for a winning recipe!

This was a great recipe. kids. love it! I made a few tweaks though. I used fresh four cheese ravioli from the refrigerator section. for the chicken I cut up into small pieces and used Italian seasoning, salt, pepper, onion powder and garlic powder. And then I cooked it in a pan with butter and 3 cloves of fresh garlic. I did this because the Alfredo sauce in the jar can be bland and I wanted the dish to have more flavor. once the meat was cooked i added the Alfredo sauce to the pan with my chicken and warmed it up. Then I layered sauce, pasta, sauce, cheese. and I did that untill I had two pans. served it with salad and garlic bread. it was awesome!

Husband and two teenage boys said this was a “restaurant quality” dish! I added sweet yellow and orange peppers, grape tomatoes?, and fresh spinach and it was amazing. Will definitely add to our meal rotation!

Why have I never had this before? It’s delicious and so easy to make! First time it was good as is, I just made it again and had no cheese so I sautéed mushrooms with the chicken, poured the sauce in the pan, mixed it all up in a casserole dish and put breadcrumbs on top. It’s amazingly good!

I made this with red sauce as alfredo is pretty high in calories. I sauteed onions, mushrooms and garlic and layered with the italian sausage ravioli and fresh spinach. I did not add chicken at all. I left out the mozarella cheese and only used some grated parm on the top, again to reduce the calories and this was very good. I made it earlier in the day and then baked later. Super easy.

This was very tasty. I used shredded chicken that I already had on hand (first I mixed in the butter and italian seasoning for maximum flavor) with chicken ravioli. Used an Italian blend cheese that had many types of cheese including parmesan so I skipped the last step of adding parmesan. I layered a few fresh spinach leaves with each layer which gave nice color. My 9 year old didn't even gripe about the spinach because I think it looked like basil in there... hmm that would be good too.

At our house 4 stars is the best. My husband gave it a 5 star! It was delicious. I made it exactly like the recipe stated except I precooked 1 cup of sliced carrots and 1 cup of peas to make it somewhat healthy! I didn't know how many cups 3 chicken breasts would be. I cook my chicken breasts ahead of time, shred and freeze in 1 cup container. I used three cups of chicken mixing the Italian seasoning with the chicken in a bowl. (No butter needed) Very fast to make and very yummy. Thanks for sharing

Great recipe and a great idea too! Tried this with a soft Gorganzola added to the homemade Alfredo sauce along with some grated fontina and parmesean cheese. Also added some garlic sautéed in the butter for the Alfredo. Sautéed chicken cutlets to layer with the raviolis. Delicious, couldn't eating it.

This is a great, simple, versatile recipe! Instead of chicken I browned sliced smoked sausage with onions and garlic. I doubled the recipe and used one jar of Alfredo sauce and one jar of traditional marinara to make an easy tomato cream sauce. It all added up to an enormous dish that the family loved!!

I make this recipe often and have for years but I usually omit the chicken and add spinach to a homemade alfredo sauce (for my vegetarian granddaughter) and ocassionaly use Johnsonville spicy Italian saugage. So many different variations possible and it's an excellant recipe. I can be made ahead of time too...

I keep jars of home canned Alfredo sauce on the shelf and I prefer it to store bought versions. I also like using shrimp or blue crab instead of chicken. Last but not least, I use home made ravioli rather than store bought. I mostly try to know what is in my food and how it was prepared. I know, I'm old school. I'm also a lot healthier than a lot of friends that are my age and younger. Anyhow, the original recipe is quite tasty and I've been told several times that my modifications are very tasty too.
Very good. I’ll make this again. I did add 8 oz. Of sliced button mushrooms & loose leaf spinach.

Are you sure this was meant for a 9x13 pan? As I was putting it together I ran out of sauce for the first layer, glad I had another jar for the seconde layer. Next time I will make it in a 9x9 pan. It's good though, I will make it another time in a smaller pan. Thank you for the recipe.
So good! I used plant based Italian sausage so good!
Definitely going to be making this a lot! Felt that the Italian seasoning was a bit much so I'll use less next time.
Great recipe, added Parmesan along with the mozzarella on each layer. Also added an extra small jar of Alfred sauce, 16 is total I’d just not enough. Will try again using spinach and shrooms.

This is one of the best recipes. I used Bertolli’s garlic Alfredo sauce and Ranna’s ravioli. I didn’t have chicken so I used some of the suggestions from other reviews; fresh mushrooms, spinach, onion and halved cherry tomatoes. I can’t wait to make it again.
